nodes.statement: The high-level strategy will be to argue that any minimizer of C_lambda^(n)(bmW) over the shifted positive semidefinite cone \bmW: bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0 \ must be within ensuremathvarepsilon sqrtdr of bm Z_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) with high probability. Let bmwidehat W := bm Z_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)- bmM, and let phi be a fixed 1-Lipschitz function. Consider the set D defined via D := bigg\ bmW :bigg| phibigg( fracbmW + bmMsqrtdrbigg) - E phibigg( fracbmwidehat W + bmMsqrtdr bigg) bigg|leq fracensuremathvarepsilon2 bigg\ cap bigg\ bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0 bigg\, and let D_ensuremathvarepsilon denote the ensuremathvarepsilon-enlargement of the set D; i.e. D_ensuremathvarepsilon := \ bmV = bmW + bmW': \| bmW' \|_F leq ensuremathvarepsilon, bmW in D\. Since by the proof of crefthm:relatecvxncvx bmZ^(lambda) is rank at most r and within radius R = C sigma sqrtdr of bmM with high probability, we will show that any rank at most r minimum of C^(n)_lambda on D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c (outside of the ensuremathvarepsilon/2 ball) but within radius R of bmM must be suboptimal with high probability, which will imply that the minimizer must lie within D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 with high probability. Carrying out this argument, in our full proof of crefthm:cvxasymptotics in crefsec:step1, we show via the Matrix CGMT that it holds that Pbigg\ arg\,min ~ &C^(n)_lambda(bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 bigg\ \\ &leq 2 Pbigg\ bmwidehat W notin D bigg\+ 2 Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)( R^dtimes d) geq L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &+ 2 Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)bigg( B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c(bmwidehat W/sqrtdr) cap \rank(bmW + M) leq r \ cap \\| bmW\|_F leq R\ bigg) leq L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\, where L_lambda^* is the quantity defined in the previous subsection. Therefore, the proof boils down to analyzing the three terms on the right hand side above. It turns out that the first two terms are straightforward to bound: the first term is exponentially small as bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)_sf ST(tau^*) is a proximal operator and hence Lipschitz. The second term is also well-behaved as L_lambda^(n) is expected to concentrate about L_lambda^* at its global minimum. The final remaining quantity is significantly more difficult to analyze. The term inside the probability can be understood as the minimum of value of L_lambda^(n) over the set of matrices bmW such that: item They are at least ensuremathvarepsilon/2 distance away from bmwidehat W; item bmW + bmM is rank at most r; item bmW has norm at most R. In order to analyze the function L_lambda^(n) over matrices such that rank(bmW + bmM) leq r , we define the auxiliary function h(bmU) &= fracgamma_n2 bigg( sqrtfrac\|bmUU^top - bmM\|_F^2n + sigma^2 frac\|bmg\|sqrtn - fraclangle bmH, bmUU^top - bmMranglen bigg)_+^2 + fraclambdadr big\ \| bmU\|_F^2 - \|bmM\|_* big\. It is straightforward to see that if bmW = bmUU^top - bmM, then h(bmU) = L_lambda^(n)(bmW). Therefore, analyzing L_lambda^(n) over rank at most r matrices is equivalent to analyzing the function h(bmU) over R^d times r. Intuitively, since L_lambda^(n)(R^d times d) is close to L_lambda^*, the optimization geometry of L_lambda^(n) should be similar to that of matrix soft-thresholding. Therefore, since h(bmU) is the ``nonconvex version'' of L_lambda^(n), the geometry of h(bmU) should behave similarly to that of nonconvex matrix factorization. Carrying out this intuition, in creflem:hstronglyconvex we show that the function h(bmU) is strongly convex on an appropriate high-probability event E_h within a region R subset R^d times r defined via R := bigg\ bmU: \| bmU - bmU^* O_bmU^*,bmU \| leq fracckappa \| bmU^* \| bigg\, where c is some universal constant, bmU^* is such that bmM = bmU^* bmU^*top, and O_bmU^*,bmU is the Frobenius-optimal orthogonal matrix aligning bmU and bmU^*. This argument is significantly different from previous analyses for the LASSO, in which the analogue of L_lambda^(n) is already strongly convex in a region near its optimal value citepmiolane_distribution_2021. In contrast, in our setting the function L_lambda^(n) need not be strongly convex near bmwidehat W, but h(bmU) can be shown to be (near bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)). This discrepancy is due to the fact that langle bmH,bmW rangle does not concentrate at rate O(sqrtdr \|bmW\|_F) uniformly over all matrices bmW (which is what is required on the event E_h for strong convexity), but langle bmH, bmUU^top - bmM rangle does concentrate at this rate uniformly over all matrices bmU. We then demonstrate that when \|bmUU^top - bmM \|_F leq R, then this automatically implies that bmU in R. Consequently, by strong convexity, we show that there is a high-probability event E_sf ST (depending only on bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)) such that if frac\|bmUU^top - bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)\|_Fsqrtdr > fracensuremathvarepsilon2, then bmU must satisfy h(bmU) > min_bmU: \|bmU- bmU^* O_bmU^*,bmU \|_F leq fracR8 \|bmU^*\| h(bmU) + Censuremathvarepsilon^2, where C is some universal constant. The above display turns out to be equivalent to the expression L_lambda^(n)bigg( B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c(bmwidehat W/sqrtdr) cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r cap \ \|bmW\|_F leq R \ bigg) > L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2, which occurs on the event E_h cap E_sf ST. Therefore, the proof is completed by tabulating the probabilities of these events.

Since by the proof of crefthm:relatecvxncvx bmZ^(lambda) is rank at most r and within radius R = C sigma sqrtdr of bmM with high probability, we will show that any rank at most r minimum of C^(n)_lambda on D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c (outside of the ensuremathvarepsilon/2 ball) but within radius R of bmM must be suboptimal with high probability, which will imply that the minimizer must lie within D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 with high probability. Carrying out this argument, in our full proof of crefthm:cvxasymptotics in crefsec:step1, we show via the Matrix CGMT that it holds that Pbigg\ arg\,min ~ &C^(n)_lambda(bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 bigg\ \\ &leq 2 Pbigg\ bmwidehat W notin D bigg\+ 2 Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)( R^dtimes d) geq L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &+ 2 Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)bigg( B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c(bmwidehat W/sqrtdr) cap \rank(bmW + M) leq r \ cap \\| bmW\|_F leq R\ bigg) leq L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\, where L_lambda^* is the quantity defined in the previous subsection. Therefore, the proof boils down to analyzing the three terms on the right hand side above. It turns out that the first two terms are straightforward to bound: the first term is exponentially small as bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)_sf ST(tau^*) is a proximal operator and hence Lipschitz. The second term is also well-behaved as L_lambda^(n) is expected to concentrate about L_lambda^* at its global minimum. The final remaining quantity is significantly more difficult to analyze. The term inside the probability can be understood as the minimum of value of L_lambda^(n) over the set of matrices bmW such that: item They are at least ensuremathvarepsilon/2 distance away from bmwidehat W; item bmW + bmM is rank at most r; item bmW has norm at most R. In order to analyze the function L_lambda^(n) over matrices such that rank(bmW + bmM) leq r , we define the auxiliary function h(bmU) &= fracgamma_n2 bigg( sqrtfrac\|bmUU^top - bmM\|_F^2n + sigma^2 frac\|bmg\|sqrtn - fraclangle bmH, bmUU^top - bmMranglen bigg)_+^2 + fraclambdadr big\ \| bmU\|_F^2 - \|bmM\|_* big\. It is straightforward to see that if bmW = bmUU^top - bmM, then h(bmU) = L_lambda^(n)(bmW). Therefore, analyzing L_lambda^(n) over rank at most r matrices is equivalent to analyzing the function h(bmU) over R^d times r. Intuitively, since L_lambda^(n)(R^d times d) is close to L_lambda^*, the optimization geometry of L_lambda^(n) should be similar to that of matrix soft-thresholding. Therefore, since h(bmU) is the ``nonconvex version'' of L_lambda^(n), the geometry of h(bmU) should behave similarly to that of nonconvex matrix factorization. Carrying out this intuition, in creflem:hstronglyconvex we show that the function h(bmU) is strongly convex on an appropriate high-probability event E_h within a region R subset R^d times r defined via R := bigg\ bmU: \| bmU - bmU^* O_bmU^*,bmU \| leq fracckappa \| bmU^* \| bigg\, where c is some universal constant, bmU^* is such that bmM = bmU^* bmU^*top, and O_bmU^*,bmU is the Frobenius-optimal orthogonal matrix aligning bmU and bmU^*. This argument is significantly different from previous analyses for the LASSO, in which the analogue of L_lambda^(n) is already strongly convex in a region near its optimal value citepmiolane_distribution_2021. In contrast, in our setting the function L_lambda^(n) need not be strongly convex near bmwidehat W, but h(bmU) can be shown to be (near bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)). This discrepancy is due to the fact that langle bmH,bmW rangle does not concentrate at rate O(sqrtdr \|bmW\|_F) uniformly over all matrices bmW (which is what is required on the event E_h for strong convexity), but langle bmH, bmUU^top - bmM rangle does concentrate at this rate uniformly over all matrices bmU. We then demonstrate that when \|bmUU^top - bmM \|_F leq R, then this automatically implies that bmU in R. Consequently, by strong convexity, we show that there is a high-probability event E_sf ST (depending only on bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)) such that if frac\|bmUU^top - bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*)\|_Fsqrtdr > fracensuremathvarepsilon2, then bmU must satisfy h(bmU) > min_bmU: \|bmU- bmU^* O_bmU^*,bmU \|_F leq fracR8 \|bmU^*\| h(bmU) + Censuremathvarepsilon^2, where C is some universal constant. The above display turns out to be equivalent to the expression L_lambda^(n)bigg( B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c(bmwidehat W/sqrtdr) cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r cap \ \|bmW\|_F leq R \ bigg) > L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2, which occurs on the event E_h cap E_sf ST. Therefore, the proof is completed by tabulating the probabilities of these events.

nodes.statement: We will argue that phibig( frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda)_sf deb big) is a Lipschitz function of bmZ^(lambda) on the event E_sf Good. Indeed, on this event, by the proof of crefthm:relatecvxncvx, it holds that \|bmZ^(lambda) - bmM \|_Fleq C sigma sqrtdr. From the condition lambda_min(bmM) geq C_0 sigma sqrtdr, Weyl's inequality implies that lambda_r(bmZ^(lambda)) geq lambda_r(bmM) - C sigma sqrtdr geq (C_0 - C) sigma sqrtdr geq lambda sqrtr, provided that C_0 is sufficiently large. From crefthm:udebzdeb, on the event E_sf Good it holds that bmZ^(lambda)_sf deb = bmV_U big( Sigma + lambda bmI big) bmV_U^top, where bmV_U are the leading r eigenvectors of bmZ^(lambda). Let eta denote the function which takes a matrix and adds lambda/sqrtdr to the leading r eigenvalues of a matrix. Then since bmZ^(lambda) = bmV_U bmSigma bmV_U^top, eta( bmZ^(lambda)/sqrtdr) = frac1sqrtdrbmV_U big( bmSigma + lambda bmI big) bmV_U^top = bmZ^(lambda)_sf deb/sqrtdr, so that eta(bmZ^(lambda)/sqrtdr) = bmZ_sf deb^(lambda)/sqrtdr. We claim that eta is Lipschitz on the set S := \bmA inR^dtimes d : lambda_r+1(bmA) =0; lambda_r(bmA) geq fraclambdasqrtd\, which contains bmZ^(lambda)/sqrtdr on the event E_sf Good. To see that eta is Lipschitz, suppose that bmA and bmB are two matrices in S, and let them have eigendecompositions bmU_A bmSigma_A bmU_A^top and bmU_B bmSigma_B bmU_B^top respectively. First, if \|bmA - bmB \|_F < lambda/sqrtd, then \| eta (bmA ) - eta (bmB) \|_F &= \| bmU_A (bmSigma + fraclambdasqrtdrbmI) bmU_A^top - bmU_B ( bmSigma_B + fraclambdasqrtdr bmI) bmU_B^top \|_F \\ &leq \| bmA - bmB \|_F +fraclambdasqrtdr \| bmU_A bmU_A^top - bmU_B bmU_B^top \|_F \\ &leq \| bmA - bmB\|_F +fraclambdasqrtdrfrac\|bmA - bmB\|_Ffraclambdasqrtd \\ &leq 2 \| bmA - bmB\|_F, where we have used the Davis-Kahan Theorem. On the other hand, if \|bmA - bmB\|_F geq lambda/sqrtd, then \| eta (bmA ) - eta (bmB) \|_F &leq \| bmA - bmB\|_F + fraclambdasqrtdr \| bmU_A bmU_A^top - bmU_B bmU_B^top \|_F \\ &leq \| bmA - bmB\|_F + frac1sqrtr \| bmA - bmB\|_F \| bmU_A bmU_A^top - bmU_B bmU_B^top \|_F \\ &leq 3 \| bmA - bmB \|_F, since the Frobenius norm of the difference of projection matrices is always at most sqrt2r. Consequently, eta is at most a 3-Lipschitz function on this set. By Kirszbaum's theorem, there exists a Lipschitz extension widetilde eta : R^dtimes d to R^dtimes d such that widetilde eta has the same Lipschitz constant of eta and widetilde eta |_S = eta. In particular, on the event E_sf Good, eta and widetilde eta coincide. Let phi be any Lipschitz function, and let widetilde phi = phi circ widetilde eta, which is also Lipschitz. By crefthm:cvxasymptotics, Pbigg\ phi bigg( &frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda)_sf deb bigg) - E phi bigg( frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)_sf ST(tau^*) bigg) > ensuremathvarepsilon bigg\ \\ &leq Pbigg\ phi bigg( frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda)_sf deb bigg) - E phi bigg( frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)_sf ST(tau^*) bigg) > ensuremathvarepsilon bigg\ cap E_sf Good + P E_sf Good^c \\ &leq Pbigg\ widetilde phi bigg( frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda) bigg) - E widetilde phi bigg( frac1sqrtdr bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)_sf ST(tau^*) bigg) > ensuremathvarepsilon bigg\ + P E_sf Good^c \\ &leq Obigg( exp( - c d) + exp( - c dr) + exp( - c n) + frac1ensuremathvarepsilon^2 exp(-c dr ensuremathvarepsilon^4 ) - exp( - frac(dr)^2n ensuremathvarepsilon^4) bigg), which completes the proof.

Let eta denote the function which takes a matrix and adds lambda/sqrtdr to the leading r eigenvalues of a matrix. Then since bmZ^(lambda) = bmV_U bmSigma bmV_U^top, eta( bmZ^(lambda)/sqrtdr) = frac1sqrtdrbmV_U big( bmSigma + lambda bmI big) bmV_U^top = bmZ^(lambda)_sf deb/sqrtdr, so that eta(bmZ^(lambda)/sqrtdr) = bmZ_sf deb^(lambda)/sqrtdr. We claim that eta is Lipschitz on the set S := \bmA inR^dtimes d : lambda_r+1(bmA) =0; lambda_r(bmA) geq fraclambdasqrtd\, which contains bmZ^(lambda)/sqrtdr on the event E_sf Good. Consequently, eta is at most a 3-Lipschitz function on this set. By Kirszbaum's theorem, there exists a Lipschitz extension widetilde eta : R^dtimes d to R^dtimes d such that widetilde eta has the same Lipschitz constant of eta and widetilde eta |_S = eta. In particular, on the event E_sf Good, eta and widetilde eta coincide. Let phi be any Lipschitz function, and let widetilde phi = phi circ widetilde eta, which is also Lipschitz. nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:Zstgoodproperties}
nodes.statement: We mimic the proof in citetcelentano_lasso_2023. First we observe that for zeta^*,tau^* fixed, the function bmH mapsto bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) is a proximal operator, and hence is tau^*-Lipschitz. Therefore, the random variable \|bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) - bmM \|_F/sqrtdr is frac(tau^*)^2dr-subgaussian. In addition, by creflem:saddlepoint, it holds that fracE \| bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) - bmM \|_F^2n = (tau^*)^2 - sigma^2 = Obigg( fracdrn sigma^2 bigg), where the last bound comes from creflem:fxdpointprops. Therefore one has fracE \| bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) - bmM \|_F^2dr &= O(1). Consequently, we see that bmH mapsto frac1dr E \| bmZ_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) - bmM \|_F^2 is (fracC_sigmadr,fracC_sigmadr) sub-Gamma by Proposition G.5 of citetmiolane_distribution_2021. Therefore, by tail bounds on sub-Gamma random variables, Pbigg\ bigg| \| bm Z_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) - bmM \|_F^2 - E \|bm Z_sf ST^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) - bmM \|_F^2 bigg| > s d r bigg\ leq C exp(- c dr (s vee s^2) ), which is what was required to show. For the other assertion, we first observe that Pbigg\ rank(bmZ^(lambda/zeta^*)(tau^*) leq r bigg\ = Pbigg\ |widehat lambda_r+1big( bmM + tau^* bmH big) |leq lambda/zeta^* bigg\. By creflem:fxdpointprops it holds that fraclambdazeta^* = fraclambda1 + O( fracd r^3/2n) geq lambda/2. Therefore, Pbigg\ |widehat lambda_r+1big( bmM + tau^* bmH big) |leq lambda/zeta^* bigg\ geq Pbigg\ |widehat lambda_r+1big( bmM + tau^* bmH big) |leq lambda/2 bigg\. By Weyl's inequality, | widehat lambda_r+1big( bmM + tau^* bmH big)| leq tau^* \| bmH \|. Since bmH is a sf GOE(d) random matrix, it holds that \| bmH \| leq 32 sqrtd with probability at least 1 - exp( - c d) for d geq C. In addition, by creflem:fxdpointprops it holds that (tau^*)^2 leq C sigma^2, where C depends only on kappa. Consequently, as long as lambda geq C_3 sigma sqrtd, for C_3 larger than some constant (possibly depending on kappa), it holds that widehat lambda_r+1( bmM + tau^* bmH) leq tau^* \|bmH \| leq C sigma sqrtdleq lambda/2. The final assertion holds by the same logic and the triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: We prove the result first for hard thresholding. First, define the event E &:= bigg\ \| bmH \| leq C sqrtd bigg\. We observe that on E, since lambda geq C_3 sigma sqrtd and tau^* leq C sigma by creflem:fxdpointprops, it holds that bmZ_sf HT^(lambda) is rank r. Consequently, on this event, phibigg( bmZ_sf HT^(lambda) bigg) &= phibigg( P_sf rank-r(bmM + tau^* bmH ) bigg) \\ &= phibigg( P_sf rank-rbigg[bmM + sigma bigg( 1 + Obig( fracdrn big)bigg) bmH bigg] bigg). Let bmU_sigma bmLambda_sigma bmU_sigma^top denote the leading rank r approximation of bmM + sigma bmH, and let bmU_tau bmLambda_tau bmU_tau^top be the leading rank r approximation of bmM + tau^* bmH. Recall that we let O_bmU_sigma,bmU_tau denote the Frobenius-optimal orthogonal matrix aligning bmU_sigma to bmU_tau. We have \| bmZ_sf HT^(lambda) - bmZ_sf HT \|_F &= \| bmU_sigma bmLambda_sigma bmU_sigma^top - bmU_tau bmLambda_tau bmU_tau^top \|_F \\ &leq \| bmU_sigma bmLambda_sigma big( bmU_sigma - bmU_tau O_bmU_tau, bmU_sigma big)^top \|_F + \| bmU_sigma big[ bmLambda_sigma O_bmU_tau,bmU_sigma^top - O_bmU_tau,bmU_sigma^top bmLambda_tau big] bmU_tau^top \|_F \\ & + \| big[ bmU_sigma O_bmU_tau,bmU_sigma^top - bmU_tau big] bmLambda_tau bmU_tau^top \|_F \\ &leq underbrace\| bmU_sigma bmLambda_sigma big( bmU_sigma - bmU_tau O_bmU_tau, bmU_sigma big)^top \|_F + \| big[ bmU_sigma O_bmU_tau,bmU_sigma^top - bmU_tau big] bmLambda_tau bmU_tau^top \|_F_=: T_1 \\ & + underbrace\| bmLambda_sigmabig[ O_bmU_tau,bmU_sigma^top - bmU_sigma^top bmU_tau big] \|_F + \| big[ bmU_sigma^top bmU_tau - O_bmU_sigma,bmU_tau big] bmLambda_tau \|_F_=:T_2 + underbrace\| bmLambda_sigmabmU_sigma^top bmU_tau - bmU_sigma^top bmU_tau bmLambda_tau \|_F_=:T_3. We will analyze each term in turn. nodes.statement: Define the Gaussian processes X(bmW,bmnu) &:= \| bmW \|_F langle bmg, bmnu rangle + \| bmnu \|langle bmH, bmW rangle; \\ Y(bmW,bmnu ) &:= langle A[bmW], bmnu rangle + \| bmnu \| \| bmW \| z, where z sim N(0,1) is independent from A(cdot), bmg is a standard Gaussian vector, and bmH is a sf GOE(d) random matrix. Observe that since bmH is sf GOE(d), langle bmH, bmW rangle sim N(0, \| bmW \|_F^2) for symmetric bmW, whence we need only define the processes for symmetric matrices bmW. We have E bigg[ Y(bmW,bmnu) Y( bmW' ,bmnu' )bigg] &- E bigg[ X(bmW,bmnu) X( bmW' ,bmnu' )bigg] \\ &= \| bmW \|_F \| bmnu \| \| bmW' \|_F \| bmnu' \| + langle bmnu, bmnu' rangle langle bmW, bmW' rangle - \| bmnu \| \|bmnu' \| langle bmW, bmW' rangle - \| bmW \|_F \|bmW' \|_F langle bmnu, bmnu' rangle \\ &= bigg( \| bmW \|_F \| bmW'\|_F - langle bmW, bmW' rangle bigg) bigg( \|bmnu \| \| bmnu' \| - langle bmnu, bmnu' rangle bigg) geq 0, with equality when bmW = bmW' or bmnu = bmnu'. Therefore, by Theorem G.2 of citetmiolane_distribution_2021, Pbigg\ min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu in S_nu Y(bmW,bmnu) + psi(bmW,bmnu) leq t bigg\ leq Pbigg\min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu in S_nu X(bmW,bmnu) + psi(bmW, bmnu) leq t bigg\. Furthermore, Pbigg\min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu inS_bmnu Y(bmW,bmnu) + psi(bmW,bmnu) leq t bigg\ &geq frac12 Pbigg\ min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu in S_bmnu Y(bmW,bmnu) + psi(bmW,bmnu) leq t | z leq 0 bigg\ \\ &geq frac12 Pbigg\ min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu in S_bmnulangle A(bmW), bmnu rangle + psi(bmW,bmnu) leq t | z leq 0 bigg\\\ &= frac12 Pbigg\ Phi(A) leq t bigg\. Rewriting the equation above yields Pbigg\ Phi(A) leq t bigg\ leq 2 Pbigg\min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu in S_bmnu X(bmW,bmnu) + psi(bmW, bmnu) leq t bigg\ = 2 P bigg\ phi(bmg,bmH) leq t bigg\. This proves the first result. Now suppose that S_bmW and S_bmnu are convex and that psi is convex-concave. Note that the argument above relies not on the minimization over S_bmW and maximization over S_bmnu -- we are free to minimize instead over S_bmnu and maximize over S_bmW. Then this argument above shows that (using -psi instead of psi) Pbigg\ min_bmnu in S_bmnumax_bmW in S_bmW langle A(bmW), bmnu rangle - psi(bmW, bmnu) leq - t bigg\ leq 2 Pbigg\ min_bmnu in S_bmnumax_bmW in S_bmW \|bmW \|_F langle bmg, bmnu rangle + \| bmnu \| langle bmH, bmW rangle - psi(bmW, bmnu) leq - t bigg\. Multiplying everything by -1 and using the fact that A (cdot), bmH, and bmg are equal in distribution to -A(cdot), - bmH and -bmg respectively yields Pbigg\ max_bmnu in S_bmnumin_bmW in S_bmW langle X(bmW), bmnu rangle + psi(bmW, bmnu) geq t bigg\ leq 2 Pbigg\ max_bmnu in S_bmnumin_bmW in S_bmW \|bmW \|_F langle bmg, bmnu rangle + \| bmnu \| langle bmH, bmW rangle + psi(bmW, bmnu) geq t bigg\. We observe that since S_bmW and S_bmnu are both convex and psi is convex-concave, by Sion's minimax theorem we are able to switch the minimum and maximum on the left hand side. For the right hand side we need not switch, but instead only observe that max_bmnu in S_bmnumin_bmW in S_bmW \|bmW \|_F langle bmg, bmnu rangle + \| bmnu \| langle bmH, bmW rangle + psi(bmW, bmnu) leq min_bmW in S_bmW max_bmnu in S_bmnu \|bmW \|_F langle bmg, bmnu rangle + \| bmnu \| langle bmH, bmW rangle + psi(bmW, bmnu). This completes the proof.

nodes.statement: First we will show that nabla^2 f^(lambda)_sf ncvx(bmU)[ bmDelta, bmDelta] is upper bounded when bmU is a critical point of f^(lambda)_sf ncvx. The proof is motivated by citetge_no_2017. nodes.statement: Observe that because C^(n)(bmW) &= frac12 \| X(bmW) - bmensuremathvarepsilon \|_F^2 + lambda \| bmW + bmM \|_* - lambda \| bmM \|_*, we need to argue that any minimizer of C^(n)(bmW) (over the shifted cone bmM + R^dtimes d_succcurlyeq 0) must must be within ensuremathvarepsilon of bmwidehat W with high probability. Let D be the set D := big\ bmW : bigg| phi big( fracbmM + bmWsqrtdrbig)- E big[ phi big( fracbmM + bmWsqrtdr big) big] bigg| leq ensuremathvarepsilon/2 big\ cap \ bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0\. Then we need to show that the minimizer of C^(n) lies within D with high probability. Let D_ensuremathvarepsilon denote the ensuremathvarepsilon-enlargement of the set D; i.e., D_ensuremathvarepsilon := \ bmW :inf_bmW'in D \|bmW - bmW'\|_F < ensuremathvarepsilon \. We will show that any rank at most r minimum of C^(n) on D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c (i.e. outside an ensuremathvarepsilon/2-region of D) must be suboptimal with high probability, which implies that the minimizer lies within D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2. To accomplish this, first note that Pbigg\ arg\,min C^(n)(bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 bigg\ &leq Pbigg\ arg\,min C^(n)( bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 cap E_sf Good bigg\ + P E_sf Good^c. Observe that the first event above satisfies bigg\ &arg\,min C^(n)( bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 cap E_sf Good bigg\\\ &subset bigg\ arg\,min C^(n)( bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r cap \| bmW \|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr bigg\ \\ &subset bigg\ exists bmW : bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0, rank(bmW + bmM) leq r, bmW notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2,\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr, \\ & C^(n) (bmW) leq min_bmW:\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) bigg\ \\ &subset bigg\ exists bmW : bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0, rank(bmW + bmM) leq r, bmW in D^c_ensuremathvarepsilon/2, \|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr, \\ & C^(n)(bmW) leq min_bmW:\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &= bigg\ min_substackbmW in D^c_ensuremathvarepsilon/2\rank(bmW + bmM) leq r\\\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) leq min_substackbmW in R^dtimes d\\bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0\\\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n) (bmW) + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\. As a result, Pbigg\ &arg\,min C^(n)(bmW) notin D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 bigg\ \\ &leq P bigg\min_substackbmW in D^c_ensuremathvarepsilon/2\rank(bmW + bmM) leq r \\ \|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) leq min_substackbmW in R^dtimes d\\ bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0\\\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n) (bmW) + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &leq Pbigg\ big\ min_substackbmW in D^c_ensuremathvarepsilon/2\rank(bmW + bmM) leq r\\\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) leq min_substackbmW in R^dtimes d \\bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0\\\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) + C ensuremathvarepsilon ^2 \ \\ & bigcap \ min_substackbmW in R^dtimes d\\ bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0\\\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) leq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 big\ bigg\ \\ & + Pbigg\ min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0,\|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr C^(n)(bmW) geq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &leq Pbigg\ min_bmW in D^c_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r C^(n)(bmW) leq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ & + Pbigg\ min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0 C^(n)(bmW) geq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &leq 2 Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)(D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r cap \|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr) leq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ & + 2Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)big(B(0,C sigma sqrtdr) big) geq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\, where the final inequality is by creflem:applycgmt. Next, note that either bmwidehat W notin D or D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c subset B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 big( bmwidehat Wbig)^c cap \ bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0 \. As a result, Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)&big( D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r) cap \|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdrbig) leq L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &leq P big\ bmwidehat W notin D big\ + Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)( B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 big( bmwidehat Wbig)^c cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r) cap \|bmW\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdrbig) leq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\. Therefore, Pbigg\& min_bmW in D_ensuremathvarepsilon/2^c C^(n)(bmW) leq min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW - bmM succcurlyeq 0 C^(n)(bmW) + C ensuremathvarepsilon ^2 bigg\ \\ &leq 2 P big\ bmwidehat W notin D big\ + 2Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n)( B_ensuremathvarepsilon/2 big( bmwidehat Wbig)^c cap rank(bmW + bmM) leq r)big) leq L^*_lambda + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ & + 2 Pbigg\ L_lambda^(n) (R^dtimes d) geq L_lambda^* + C ensuremathvarepsilon^2 bigg\ \\ &leq 2 P big\ bmwidehat W notin D big\ + Obigg( exp( - c d) + exp( - c dr) + exp( - c n) + frac1ensuremathvarepsilon^2 exp(-c dr ensuremathvarepsilon^4 ) - exp( - frac(dr)^2n ensuremathvarepsilon^4) bigg), where we have applied creflem:concentrationlemma. Note that by construction bmW + bmM succcurlyeq 0 almost surely. In addition, we have that the soft-thresholding operator is a proximal operator and hence nonexpansive, implying it is 1-Lipschitz. As a result, the function frac1sqrtdr bmM - fractau^*sqrtdr bmH mapsto bmwidehat W is a tau^*/sqrtdr Lipschitz function of bmH. Therefore, Pbig\ bmwidehat W notin D big\ &leq 2 exp big\ - c fracd r ensuremathvarepsilon^2tau^* big\. By creflem:fxdpointprops, sigma leq tau^* leq C sigma , and hence by adjusting constants if necessary, we complete the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:applycgmt}
nodes.statement: The proof amounts to rewriting the appropriate quantities. We have that min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW+M succcurlyeq 0 cap D C_lambda^(n) (bmW) &= min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW+M succcurlyeq 0 cap D frac12\| X[bmW] - bmensuremathvarepsilon \|_F^2 + lambda \| bmW + bmM \|_* \\ &=min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW+M succcurlyeq 0 cap Dmax_bmnu in R^n langle X[bmW], bmnu rangle - langle bmensuremathvarepsilon , bmnu rangle - frac12 \| bmnu \|^2 + lambda \| bmW + bmM\|_*. Furthermore, observe that C_lambda^(n)(bmW) is convex and satisfies C_lambda^(n)(bmW) to infty as \|bmW \|_Fto infty, and hence admits minimizers. Therefore, there exists a constant M sufficiently large such that the maximizer nu is bounded with \|bmnu \| leq M. As a result, since the min-max is attained on a closed set, we may apply the MCGMT to deduce that Pbigg\ & min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW+M succcurlyeq 0 cap D C_lambda^(n) (bmW) > t bigg\ \\ &leq 2 P bigg\ min_bmW in R^dtimes d: bmW+M succcurlyeq 0 cap Dmax_bmnu in R^n \| bmW \|_F langle bmg, bmnu rangle /sqrtn +\| bmnu\| langle bmH, bmW rangle /sqrtn- langle bmensuremathvarepsilon, bmnu rangle - frac12 \| bmnu \|^2 + lambda \| bmW + bmM \|_* > t bigg\, where the final equality is due to the fact that -langle bmensuremathvarepsilon,bmnurangle - frac12 \|bmnu\|^2 is concave (and hence the function (bmW,bmnu) mapsto -langle bmensuremathvarepsilon,bmnurangle - frac12 \|bmnu\|^2 + lambda \|bmW\|_* is convex-concave). Here bmg is a standard Gaussian random vector and bmH is a GOE matrix. The first equality follows from the fact that frac12\|bmv \|_2^2 = max_bmnu langle bmv,bmnu rangle - frac12 \|bmnu\|^2. Since the statement is probabilistic in nature, we are free to make the replacement bmH mapsto - bmH by symmetry. Diving the resulting expressions inside the probability by dr and recognizing that the right hand side is simply psi^(n)_lambda(bmW,bmnu), we complete the proof (after rescaling t by dr). The reverse inequality follows by the same argument.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:Eh_highprob}
nodes.statement: The proof follows via ensuremathvarepsilon-net. Let bmA be any rank at most 2r matrix such that \|bmA\|_Fleq 1. Then langle bmH, bmA rangle is Gaussian with variance at most 2 \|bmA\|_F^2 leq 2. Hoeffding's inequality implies that bigg| langle bmH,bmA rangle bigg| leq C t with probability at least 1 - 2 exp( - c t^2). Next, let N_ensuremathvarepsilon be a covering of rank at most 2r matrices of Frobenius norm at most 1; by Lemma 3.1 of citetcandes_tight_2011, it holds that |N_ensuremathvarepsilon| leq bigg( frac9ensuremathvarepsilon bigg)^3 dr. The union bound implies that sup_bmA in N_ensuremathvarepsilon bigg| langle bmH,bmA rangle bigg| leq C t with probability at least 1 - 2exp( 3dr log (9/ensuremathvarepsilon) - t^2 ). Taking t geq sqrtdr shows that this probability is at most 1 - 2 exp( - c d r) as desired. For the other event it holds that frac\|bmg\|sqrtn is a frac1sqrtn-Lipschitz function of bmg and consequently the event holds with probability at least 1 - 2exp( - c n). The bound on \|bmH\| follows directly from citetbandeira_sharp_2016.

Note that $\bm{U}^{(\lambda)}$ satisfies
\begin{align}
  \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i}  \bigg( \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i , \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle / \sqrt{n} - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg) \bm{X}_i \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} + \lambda \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} = 0,
\end{align}
which shows that $\bm{U}^{(\lambda)}_{({\sf deb})}$ satisfies
\begin{align}
\nabla f^{(0)}_{{\sf ncvx}}&( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)}_{{\sf deb}} ) \\
& =   \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}  \sum_{i}  \bigg\{ \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i , \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg) (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle /\sqrt{n}- \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg\} \bm{X}_i \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &=  \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{i}  \bigg\{ \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i , \bm{U}^{(\lambda)}  (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle/\sqrt{n} - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg\} \bm{X}_i \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &\quad+ \frac{\lambda}{n} \sum_{i} \bigg\{ \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i , \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1}  (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top}  \bigg \rangle  \bigg\} \bm{X}_i \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i}  \bigg\{ \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i , \bm{U}^{(\lambda)}  (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle /\sqrt{n}- \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg\} \bm{X}_i \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &\quad+ \lambda \mathcal{X}^* \mathcal{X} \bigg( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big( ( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)} )^{\top}  \bigg) \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &= -\lambda \bm{U}^{(\lambda)}  \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &\quad + \lambda \bigg( \mathcal{X}^* \mathcal{X} - \mathcal{I} \bigg) \bigg[ \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big( (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top}  \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bigg] \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2}  \\
      &\quad + \lambda \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} \\
      &= \lambda \bigg( \mathcal{X}^* \mathcal{X} - \mathcal{I} \bigg) \bigg[ \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big( (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top}  \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} (\bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bigg] \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \bigg( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)})^{\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \bigg)^{1/2} .
\end{align}
Taking norms, we obtain that
\begin{align}
    \| \nabla f^{(0)}_{{\sf ncvx}} \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)}_{{\sf deb}} \big) \|_F &\leq \lambda \big\| \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big( \bm{I} + \lambda \big( \bm{U}^{(\lambda)\top} \bm{U}^{(\lambda)} \big)^{-1} \big)^{1/2}  \big\|_F \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{X}^* \mathcal{X} - \mathcal{I} \bigg) \big(  \bm{V}_U \bm{V}_U^{\top} \big)\bigg \| \\
    &= \lambda \| \bm{U}^{(\lambda)}_{{\sf deb}} \|_F \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{X}^* \mathcal{X} - \mathcal{I} \bigg) \big(  \bm{V}_U \bm{V}_U^{\top} \big)\bigg\|.
\end{align}
 By \cref{lem:netargument}, we have that with the advertised probability,
\begin{align}
    \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{X}^* \mathcal{X} - \mathcal{I} \bigg) \big(  \bm{V}_U \bm{V}_U^{\top} \big)\bigg \| &\lesssim \frac{r \sqrt{d}}{\sqrt{n}},
\end{align}
whence the proof is completed.

nodes.statement: We observe that sf vec(bmU^(0) - bmU_sf deb^(lambda) )^top nabla^2 f^(0)_sf ncvxbig( t bmU^(0) + (1 - t) bmU^(lambda)_sf deb big)sf vec(bmU^(0) - bmU_sf deb^(lambda) ) &= nabla^2 f^(0)_sf ncvx bigg( t bmU^(0) + (1-t) bmU_sf deb^(lambda) bigg)[ bmV, bmV], with bmV = bmU^(0) - bmU_sf deb^(lambda), where we have already assumed (without loss of generality) that O_bmU^(0), bmU_sf deb^(lambda) = bmI_r. Let bmU = t bmU^(0) + (1 - t) bmU^(lambda)_sf deb. By creflem:convexitydeterministic, on the event E_creflem:secondderivcloseness it holds that nabla^2 f^(0)_sf ncvx big( bmU big)[ bmV, bmV] geq lambda_min(bmU)^2\| bmV\|_F^2 bigg( 1 - frac\| bmUU^top - bmM\| + 2 delta_2r \|bmU\|^2 + delta_2r \| bmUU^top \|_F + delta_2r \| bmM \| + C sigma sqrtdrlambda_min(bmU)^2 bigg). To complete the proof of the lower bound we need only bound the numerator above. item Step 1: Studying bmU^(0) and bmU_sf deb^(lambda): Through an argument similar to the proof of creflem:uncvxgood (take lambda = 0 therein) shows that on the event E_sf Good \| bmU^(0) bmU^(0)top - bmM \|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr. Therefore, Weyl's inequality shows that lambda_min(bmU^(0))^2 &= lambda_min(bmU^(0) bmU^(0)top) geq lambda_min(bmM) - C sigma sqrtdr geq fraclambda_min(bmM)2, which holds by crefass1. We now consider bmU_sf deb^(lambda). We have that by crefthm:udebzdeb it holds that on the event E_sf Good bmU_sf deb^(lambda) bmU_sf deb^(lambda)top = bmZ_sf deb^(lambda) = bmV_Ubig( bmSigma + lambda bmI big) bmV_U^top. Furthermore, on this same event, by crefthm:relatecvxncvx it holds that \| bmZ^(lambda) - bmM \|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr. Consequently, it holds that \|bmU_sf deb^(lambda) bmU_sf deb^(lambda)top - bmM\|_F leq C sigma sqrtdr. Therefore, the same argument shows that lambda_min(bmU_sf deb^(lambda))^2 geq fraclambda_min(bmM)2. The triangle inequality also shows that \|bmU_sf deb^(lambda)\|^2 leq \| bmM \| + \|bmU_sf deb^(lambda) bmU_sf deb^(lambda)top - bmM\|_F leq 2 \| bmM \|. The same bound holds for bmU^(0) as well. item Step 2: Bounding bmU. As a consequence of the previous step, we have that lambda_min(bmU)^2 &= lambda_minbigg( t bmU^(0) + (1 - t) bmU^(lambda)_sf deb bigg)^2 \\ &= lambda_min bigg( t^2 bmU^(0)top bmU^(0) + (1 - t)^2 bmU_sf deb^(lambda)top bmU_sf deb^(lambda) + t(1-t) bmU^(0)topbmU_sf deb^(lambda)+ t(1-t)bmU_sf deb^(lambda)topbmU^(0) bigg) \\ &geq fract^22 lambda_min(bmM) + frac(1 - t)^22 lambda_min(bmM) + 2 t(1-t) lambda_min(bmU_sf deb^(lambda)topbmU^(0)) \\ &geq fract^2 + (1-t)^22 lambda_min(bmM) \\ &geq fraclambda_min(bmM)8, where we have recognized that bmU_sf deb^(lambda)topbmU^(0) is a positive diagonal matrix by the fact that they are already aligned. A similar argument gives \| bmU \|^2 leq 4 \| bmM \|. By Lemma 6 of citetge_no_2017 it holds that \| bmU^(0) O_bmU^(0),bmU^* - bmU^* \|_F leq frac12 lambda_min^1/2(bmM) \| bmU^(0) bmU^(0)top - bmM \|_F leq fracC sigma sqrtdr2lambda_min^1/2(bmM). item Step 3: Bounding bmUU^top - bmM. First, define the set B_x(bmU^*) := \ bmU: \| bmU O_bmU,bmU^* - bmU^* \|_F leq x \. We note that B_x(bmU^*) is the geodesic ball on the Riemannian quotient space [bmU] := \ bmU O: OO^top = bmI_r \. By Theorem 2 of citetluo_nonconvex_2022, the set B_x(bmU^*) is geodesically convex for any x leq lambda_min(bmU^*)/3. Moreover, by Lemma 2 of citetluo_nonconvex_2022 the function bmU(t) := bmU_sf deb^(lambda) + t big( bmU^(0) - bmU_sf deb^(lambda) big) is the unique minimizing geodesic from [bmU_sf deb^(lambda)] to [bmU^(0)] (where we have used the fact that without loss of generality both matrices are already properly aligned). Since both bmU^(0) and bmU_sf deb^(lambda) are full rank from the previous arguments, it holds that [bmU] in B_x(bmU^*). In particular, it holds that \| bmU(t) O_bmU,bmU^* - bmU^* \|_F leq fracC sigma sqrtdr2lambda_min^1/2(bmM). for all t. Lemma 11 of citetluo_nonconvex_2022 shows that \| bmUU^top - bmM \| leq sqrtkappa C sigma sqrtdr leq fraclambda_min(bmM)10, where the final bound follows from crefass1. Combining these bounds we have that on the event E_sf Good \| bmUU^top - bmM \| + 2 delta_2r \| bmU \|^2 + delta_2r \| bmUU^top\|_F + delta_2r \| bmM \| + C sigma sqrtdr &leq sqrtkappa C sigma sqrtdr + 8 fracc_0sqrtr \| bmM \| + 4 c_0 \| bmM\| + C sigma sqrtdr \\ &leq C' sigma sqrtdr + C' c_0 \| bmM \| \\ &leq fraclambda_min(bmM)20 provided c_0 is smaller than some constant, where c_0 is such that delta_2r leq fracc_0sqrtr. Therefore, nabla^2 f(bmU)[bmV,bmV] geqfraclambda_min(bmM)8 \|bmV \|_F^2 big( 1 - frac25 big) geq fraclambda_min(bmM)20 \|bmV \|_F^2 as desired. The upper bound follows from a similar argument.

nodes.raw_latex:
The hessian satisfies
\begin{align}
    \nabla^2 f^{(0)}_{{\sf ncvx}}(\bm{U})[\bm{V},\bm{V}] &= \frac{d}{dt} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle \bm{X}_i, \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big) \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big), \bm{V} \bigg\rangle .
\end{align}
We have that
\begin{align}
     \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle &\bm{X}_i, \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big) \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big), \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
     &=  \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle \bm{X}_i, \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big) \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big), \bm{V} \bigg\rangle  - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i\bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big), \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
     &=  \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle \bm{X}_i, \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big) \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i  \bm{U} , \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
     &\quad+ t \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle \bm{X}_i, \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big) \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i  \bm{V} , \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
     &\quad  - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i\bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big), \bm{V} \bigg\rangle
     \\
     &=  \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle \bm{X}_i,  \bm{U}  \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i  \bm{U} , \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
&\quad +     t \bigg[\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg\langle \bm{X}_i,   \bm{V}  \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} \bigg \rangle \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i  \bm{U} , \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
     &\quad+ t \bigg[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg\langle \bm{X}_i, \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big) \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big)^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle \bigg] \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i  \bm{V} , \bm{V} \bigg\rangle \\
     &\quad  - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i\bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \big( \bm{U} + t \bm{V} \big), \bm{V} \bigg\rangle
\end{align}
Taking only terms linear in $t$ yields that
\begin{align}
    \nabla^2 f^{(0)}_{{\sf ncvx}}(\bm{U})[ \bm{V}, \bm{V}] &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i, \bm{U W}^{\top} + \bm{VU}^{\top}  \bigg \rangle \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \bm{U}, \bm{V} \bigg \rangle + \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg \langle \bm{X}_i , \bm{UU}^{\top} - \bm{M} \bigg \rangle \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \bm{V}, \bm{V} \bigg \rangle  \\
    &\quad - \ensuremath{\varepsilon}_i \bigg \langle \bm{X}_i \bm{V}, \bm{V} \bigg \rangle 
\end{align}
as desired.

nodes.statement: First, we write nabla^2 f^(0)_sf ncvx(bmU)[bmV, bmV] := nabla^2 f^(sf clean)(bmU)[bmV, bmV] - frac1sqrtn sum_i=1^nensuremathvarepsilon_i bigg langle bmX_i bmV, bmV bigg rangle, where nabla^2 f^(sf clean)(bmU)[bmV, bmV] &= frac1n sum_i=1^n bigg langle bmX_i, bmU V^top + bmVU^top bigg rangle bigg langle bmX_i bmU, bmV bigg rangle + bigg langle bmX_i , bmUU^top - bmM bigg rangle bigg langle bmX_i bmV, bmV bigg rangle. First we bound the difference between nabla^2 f^sf clean and nabla^2 f^sf MF, uniformly over matrices of rank at most 2r. Lemma 3 of citetchi_nonconvex_2019 shows that if X satisfies the restricted isometry property with constant delta_2r, then bigg| frac1n sum_i=1^n langle bmX_i, bmQ_1 rangle langle bmX_i, bmQ_2 rangle - langle bmQ_1, bmQ_2 rangle bigg| &leq delta_2r \| bmQ_1 \|_F \| bmQ_2\|_F, uniformly over matrices bmQ_1, bmQ_2 of rank at most r. Consequently, when the restricted isometry property holds, by breaking up the sum it holds that bigg| nabla^2 f^(sf clean)(bmU)[bmV, bmV] - nabla^2 f^sf MF(bmU)[bmV, bmV] bigg| &leq delta_2r bigg( 2\| bmUV^top \|_F^2 + \| bmUU^top \|_F \| bmVV^top \|_F + \| bmM \|_F \| bmVV^top \|_F bigg) \\ &leq delta_2r \| bmV\|_F^2 bigg( 2 \| bmU \|^2 + \| bmUU^top \|_F + \| bmM \|_F bigg). We now bound the noise term. Observe that for fixed matrix bmVV^top of rank at most r, it holds that frac1sqrtn sum_i=1^n ensuremathvarepsilon_i bigg langle bmX_i ,bmV bmV^top bigg rangle &oversetd= frac \| bmV bmV^top \|_Fsqrtn langle bmensuremathvarepsilon, bmZ rangle, where bmZ and bmensuremathvarepsilon/sigma are standard Gaussian random vectors. Standard concentration arguments show that for fixed matrix bmVV^top, conditional on bmensuremathvarepsilon, bigg| frac1sqrtn sum_i=1^n ensuremathvarepsilon_i bigg langle bmX_i ,bmV bmV^top bigg rangle bigg| &leq C sigma \| bmVV^top \|_F frac\| bmensuremathvarepsilon \|sqrtn s with probability at least 1 - 2exp(-c s^2). Recognizing that \| bmensuremathvarepsilon \|/sqrtn leq C with probability at least 1 - 2 exp( - c n) shows that for any fixed bmV it holds that bigg| frac1sqrtn sum_i=1^n ensuremathvarepsilon_i bigg langle bmX_i ,bmV bmV^top bigg rangle bigg| &leq C sigma \| bmVV^top \|_F s with probability at least 1 - 2 exp(- c s^2) - 2 exp( - c n). Taking s asymp sqrtdr and a standard net argument shows that this bound holds uniformly over matrices bmVV^top of rank at most r with probability at least 1 - O( exp( - c dr ) ).
